text:
sam: Hey folks — pinging runtime/platform/infra/sec for quick eyes on PR #52234. This changes the eviction retry/backoff window that lives in the runtime cache layer. Short blurb: reduced aggressive retries that were causing thrash under GC-heavy workloads; could affect cold-start/fallback behavior. https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/52234 :eyes:

sam: Key files: runtime/cache/eviction.go, orch/policy/eviction_config.yaml. Unit tests added + an integration test that simulates memory pressure.

sam: Config diff (core change):
```yaml
eviction:
  base_retry_ms: 50  # was 10
  max_backoff_ms: 2000  # was 5000
  jitter_pct: 0.15
```

sam: Why I need specific teams: runtime — verify correctness/perf; platform — canary + rollout plan; infra — any infra-level signals we should watch (OOMs, node eviction); security — confirm no new surface for secrets/KMS etc.

alex: I can take a runtime look tomorrow morning. Can you paste the perf numbers you saw with the old vs new config?

sam: perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood-inference/internal/d/eviction/eviction-retry?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now — short summary: token-latency 95p improved ~4% under sustained eviction, p99 unchanged. CPU transient spikes reduced.

alex: nice. Any regressions on cold-start fallbacks?

sam: lab sim shows slightly slower immediate second-retry which reduced repeated requeues; overall fewer duplicate inflight requests. TL;DR: better stability at cost of one extra ms for rare path.

ben: runtime note — this touches the hot path for KV cache. unit tests look ok but needs one more test around concurrent aborts. I can add that to the PR if folks are fine with the change.

maria: security — quick Q: does this modify any auth headers, KMS calls, or telemetry that could leak info?

sam: No KMS/auth changes. Telemetry: we emit a metric `eviction.retry_count` and `eviction.backoff_ms` (already existed) — same names, just different values. I added labels for `policy:reduced-thrash` for tracing. Nothing sensitive.

maria: OK, thanks. will sign off once runtime confirms no increased surface. :thumbsup:

rachel: platform — what canary window do you propose? Also any rollback trigger?
sam: Proposal: 1% traffic for 2 hours, watch `eviction.retries` and `request_duplicated` metrics, p95 latency. Rollback if `request_duplicated` increases by >25% or p95 latency increases >5% for 10m. Canary script attached in PR description.

rachel: sounds reasonable. pls add a note in the canary runbook about node-level OOM alerts (ops page).

sam: Will add.

alex: quick runtime findings after grep through code: change looks safe but one minor nit in comment block; otherwise :+1: pending ben's extra test.

ben: pushed a small test commit to the branch. CI kicked off.

ci-bot: CI passed — all checks green for branch `eviction/retry-tuning` (sha abc1234).

runtime-bot: Deploy plan staged. Canary job scheduled in 10m (owner: rachel).

sam: Thanks all. If runtime + platform + infra + sec are happy, can we get an approval? tagging @alex @rachel @maria @ben.

alex: approved. :white_check_mark:

maria: approved. :white_check_mark:

rachel: approving canary and will watch. added ops note.

ben: lgtm — merged after CI.

sam: merged. Will post post-canary notes after 2h. Thanks everyone! :party_popper:
